hero.headline: C-23 Canal diversion project in Martin County complete, rerouting billions of gallons from St. Lucie Estuary
hero.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, calling it part of the largest environmental restor
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, calling it part of the largest environmental restoration effort in U.S. history. The project will reroute excess water from the C-23 Canal away from the South Fork of the Saint Lucie River and send it through a nearly 7-mile interconnect canal to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area.

 Since entering its operational testing phase in May, the project has diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary. The pump station is capable of moving 166 million gallons of water every day and has been operational since May 14. When operating at full capacity, the pump stations can fill an Olympic-size swimming pool in just under 6 minutes.

 Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the project is projected to prevent 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the Saint Lucie River on average each year, and will divert 6.3 billion gallons of water from the river to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area. The project is located at 10297 Southwest Martin Highway and addresses excess water that had previously contributed to harmful algal blooms in the river.

 DeSantis said his administration has invested close to $10 billion in Everglades restoration and water quality since taking office in January 2019. He said his administration has completed or broken ground on more than 90 Everglades projects and cited reductions of 5.6 million pounds of nitrogen per year and nearly 1 million pounds of phosphorus per year as among the tangible results of those investments.

 DeSantis was joined at the ribbon-cutting by Lambert and South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett, along with district board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr. Lambert pointed to measurable environmental improvements since DeSantis took office, including seagrass returning to stable levels in the Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary, supporting fish and manatee populations as well as the ecotourism industry.

cards.headline: Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo's animal cruelty trial delayed to 2027
cards.teaser: The trial for Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo has been pushed to 2027 after at least a ninth continuance, with a key state witness on medical disability unable to testify until late January. The defense has also filed a motion to dismiss the case entirely.
cards.body:
The trial for Palm City dog trainer and boarder Nikki Camerlengo has been delayed until 2027, marking at least the ninth continuance in a case that began more than two years ago. In court Wednesday morning, prosecutor Kristin Chase told Judge Elizabeth Metzger that one of the state's key witnesses is on medical disability and cannot testify until at least the end of January, according to doctors.

 That witness must first testify at a hearing to determine whether she will be allowed to take the stand at trial. Metzger is now aiming for February for that hearing, pushing any potential trial date even further back.

 Camerlengo faces two counts of animal cruelty in the deaths of two dogs that died while in the care of her Palm City training and boarding facility, Pawsitively Paradise. She was arrested in 2024 after Martin County detectives said the dogs died in her care. A WPTV investigation linked at least seven dog deaths or serious injuries to Pawsitively Paradise over the course of a decade.

 Her attorneys filed a motion to dismiss the case on Sept. 2, and Metzger ordered both sides to set a hearing on that motion by the end of this week. Camerlengo's next court date is set for December, though the judge could take up the motion to dismiss sooner. Defense attorney Stuart Kaplan has asked the court to block testimony from both the Texas veterinary pathologist who performed the two necropsies and from lead investigator Detective Christine Polizzi.

 Kaplan told WPTV he believes the detective did not have all of the facts. The hearing to decide whether those witnesses can testify has not yet taken place.

 The latest delay comes after a contentious July 2026 hearing in which Metzger pressed both the prosecution and defense over why the case still hadn't gone to trial. At one point, an exchange between Metzger and Kaplan grew heated. At that hearing, Metzger said the case had been continued so many times she had lost count.

 For Adele Kirk Csontos, the wait for justice started even before Camerlengo's arrest. She filed a police report after her dog, Mako, died following 48 hours at Pawsitively Paradise in November 2022. Camerlengo was never charged in Mako's death because his necropsy was inconclusive.

 Necropsies of two other dogs concluded they died from blunt force trauma, leading to her arrest and charges. Kirk Csontos said she did not think it would be two years. Despite the ongoing delays, Kirk Csontos said she is still hopeful that Camerlengo will be held accountable.

cards.headline: Judge denies bond reduction for ex-Fort Pierce officer who searched databases 382 times
cards.teaser: A judge denied a request to lower the $80,000 bond for Josepher Crutchfield, who faces four felony counts for allegedly using law enforcement databases to track his ex-girlfriend more than 400 times.
cards.body:
A judge denied a bond reduction request Wednesday for former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield, who faces four felony counts of unauthorized computer access after investigators say he tracked his ex-girlfriend by searching law enforcement databases more than 400 times. Crutchfield appeared at his first court appearance where his attorney asked the judge to reduce his bond from $80,000, but the state successfully argued the bond should remain in place.

 Police say Crutchfield accessed the department's Flock license plate cameras and other law enforcement databases more than 400 times to track his ex-girlfriend's car, with 382 of those searches conducted through Flock cameras. Authorities said most of the searches occurred while Crutchfield was off duty, allowing him to see where and when her car was spotted.

 An assistant state attorney told the court that law enforcement officers entrusted with these duties should be the first not to abuse them, particularly given national concerns about Flock cameras. The prosecutor cited concerns about public trust in Flock cameras as a reason to keep the bond at its current level.

 Crutchfield faces four third-degree felony counts, each carrying a $20,000 warrant. He resigned from the Fort Pierce Police Department last month after learning he was under investigation. His bond remains set at $80,000.

hero.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, calling it part of the largest environmental restor
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, calling it part of the largest environmental restoration effort in U.S. history. The project will reroute excess water from the C-23 Canal away from the South Fork of the Saint Lucie River and send it through a nearly 7-mile interconnect canal to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area.

 Since entering its operational testing phase in May, the project has diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary. The pump station is capable of moving 166 million gallons of water every day and has been operational since May 14. When operating at full capacity, the pump stations can fill an Olympic-size swimming pool in just under 6 minutes.

 Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the project is projected to prevent 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the Saint Lucie River on average each year, and will divert 6.3 billion gallons of water from the river to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area. The project is located at 10297 Southwest Martin Highway and addresses excess water that had previously contributed to harmful algal blooms in the river.

 DeSantis said his administration has invested close to $10 billion in Everglades restoration and water quality since taking office in January 2019. He said his administration has completed or broken ground on more than 90 Everglades projects and cited reductions of 5.6 million pounds of nitrogen per year and nearly 1 million pounds of phosphorus per year as among the tangible results of those investments.

 DeSantis was joined at the ribbon-cutting by Lambert and South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett, along with district board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr. Lambert pointed to measurable environmental improvements since DeSantis took office, including seagrass returning to stable levels in the Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary, supporting fish and manatee populations as well as the ecotourism industry.

hero.headline: C-23 Canal diversion project in Martin County complete, rerouting billions of gallons from St. Lucie Estuary
hero.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, calling it part of the largest environmental restor
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, calling it part of the largest environmental restoration effort in U.S. history. The project will reroute excess water from the C-23 Canal away from the South Fork of the Saint Lucie River and send it through a nearly 7-mile interconnect canal to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area.

 Since entering its operational testing phase in May, the project has diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary. The pump station is capable of moving 166 million gallons of water every day and has been operational since May 14. When operating at full capacity, the pump stations can fill an Olympic-size swimming pool in just under 6 minutes.

 Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the project is projected to prevent 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the Saint Lucie River on average each year, and will divert 6.3 billion gallons of water from the river to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area. The project is located at 10297 Southwest Martin Highway and addresses excess water that had previously contributed to harmful algal blooms in the river.

 DeSantis said his administration has invested close to $10 billion in Everglades restoration and water quality since taking office in January 2019. He said his administration has completed or broken ground on more than 90 Everglades projects and cited reductions of 5.6 million pounds of nitrogen per year and nearly 1 million pounds of phosphorus per year as among the tangible results of those investments.

 DeSantis was joined at the ribbon-cutting by Lambert and South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett, along with district board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr. Lambert pointed to measurable environmental improvements since DeSantis took office, including seagrass returning to stable levels in the Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary, supporting fish and manatee populations as well as the ecotourism industry.

cards.headline: Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo's animal cruelty trial delayed to 2027
cards.teaser: The trial for Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo has been pushed to 2027 after at least a ninth continuance, with a key state witness on medical disability unable to testify until late January. The defense has also filed a motion to dismiss the case entirely.
cards.body:
The trial for Palm City dog trainer and boarder Nikki Camerlengo has been delayed until 2027, marking at least the ninth continuance in a case that began more than two years ago. In court Wednesday morning, prosecutor Kristin Chase told Judge Elizabeth Metzger that one of the state's key witnesses is on medical disability and cannot testify until at least the end of January, according to doctors.

 That witness must first testify at a hearing to determine whether she will be allowed to take the stand at trial. Metzger is now aiming for February for that hearing, pushing any potential trial date even further back.

 Camerlengo faces two counts of animal cruelty in the deaths of two dogs that died while in the care of her Palm City training and boarding facility, Pawsitively Paradise. She was arrested in 2024 after Martin County detectives said the dogs died in her care. A WPTV investigation linked at least seven dog deaths or serious injuries to Pawsitively Paradise over the course of a decade.

 Her attorneys filed a motion to dismiss the case on Sept. 2, and Metzger ordered both sides to set a hearing on that motion by the end of this week. Camerlengo's next court date is set for December, though the judge could take up the motion to dismiss sooner. Defense attorney Stuart Kaplan has asked the court to block testimony from both the Texas veterinary pathologist who performed the two necropsies and from lead investigator Detective Christine Polizzi.

 Kaplan told WPTV he believes the detective did not have all of the facts. The hearing to decide whether those witnesses can testify has not yet taken place.

 The latest delay comes after a contentious July 2026 hearing in which Metzger pressed both the prosecution and defense over why the case still hadn't gone to trial. At one point, an exchange between Metzger and Kaplan grew heated. At that hearing, Metzger said the case had been continued so many times she had lost count.

 For Adele Kirk Csontos, the wait for justice started even before Camerlengo's arrest. She filed a police report after her dog, Mako, died following 48 hours at Pawsitively Paradise in November 2022. Camerlengo was never charged in Mako's death because his necropsy was inconclusive.

 Necropsies of two other dogs concluded they died from blunt force trauma, leading to her arrest and charges. Kirk Csontos said she did not think it would be two years. Despite the ongoing delays, Kirk Csontos said she is still hopeful that Camerlengo will be held accountable.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie mayor says infrastructure remains top priority as Gatlin Boulevard work advances
cards.teaser: Mayor Shannon Martin highlighted several Gatlin Boulevard projects approved by the City Council, including resurfacing and intersection improvements beginning this month.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin says infrastructure remains a top priority for the city, pointing to several recently approved projects along Gatlin Boulevard aimed at improving traffic flow, roadway conditions and safety.

 In a community email, Martin highlighted three projects along the busy corridor that were approved by the Port St. Lucie City Council. Two are scheduled to begin this month, while another remains in final design with construction anticipated in 2027.

 Gatlin Boulevard resurfacing to begin this month

 The city plans to resurface Gatlin Boulevard from SW Edgarce Street to SW Brighton Street.

 According to Martin, the project is intended to extend the life of the roadway and improve driving conditions along the corridor.

 The resurfacing work is scheduled to begin this month, with much of the construction expected to take place at night in an effort to limit disruptions for drivers, nearby residents and businesses.

 The project is being funded through Port St. Lucie's voter-approved Half-Cent Sales Tax, which provides funding for transportation and infrastructure improvements throughout the city.

 Changes planned at Gatlin and Brighton

 The city is also moving forward with intersection improvements at Gatlin Boulevard and SW Brighton Street.

 Plans include closing the existing median opening and extending eastbound turn lanes. Martin said the changes are designed to improve both safety and traffic flow through the intersection.

 The Brighton Street improvements are expected to begin alongside the Gatlin Boulevard resurfacing work this month, with most construction again scheduled during nighttime hours.

 Gatlin and Savona improvements expected in 2027

 A third project will focus on the intersection of Gatlin Boulevard and SW Savona Boulevard.

 The planned work includes additional and extended turn lanes along with roadway improvements on Savona Boulevard.

 That project is currently in the final design stage, according to Martin. Construction is anticipated to begin in summer 2027.

 Martin described the projects as important investments in Port St. Lucie's roadway infrastructure, particularly along Gatlin Boulevard, one of the city's heavily traveled corridors.

 "These are important investments in our roadway infrastructure and will help make this busy corridor safer and easier to navigate," Martin wrote in the community update.

 The projects come as Port St. Lucie continues to contend with the transportation demands created by years of population and development growth, making roadway capacity, maintenance and intersection improvements an increasingly visible issue for residents.

 Residents can find additional information about the projects and Port St. Lucie's roadway preservation program on the City of Port St. Lucie repaving website .

hero.headline: Judge denies bond reduction for ex-Fort Pierce officer who searched databases 382 times
hero.teaser: A judge denied a request to lower the $80,000 bond for Josepher Crutchfield, who faces four felony counts for allegedly using law enforcement databases to track his ex-girlfriend more than 400 times.
hero.body:
A judge denied a bond reduction request Wednesday for former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield, who faces four felony counts of unauthorized computer access after investigators say he tracked his ex-girlfriend by searching law enforcement databases more than 400 times. Crutchfield appeared at his first court appearance where his attorney asked the judge to reduce his bond from $80,000, but the state successfully argued the bond should remain in place.

 Police say Crutchfield accessed the department's Flock license plate cameras and other law enforcement databases more than 400 times to track his ex-girlfriend's car, with 382 of those searches conducted through Flock cameras. Authorities said most of the searches occurred while Crutchfield was off duty, allowing him to see where and when her car was spotted.

 An assistant state attorney told the court that law enforcement officers entrusted with these duties should be the first not to abuse them, particularly given national concerns about Flock cameras. The prosecutor cited concerns about public trust in Flock cameras as a reason to keep the bond at its current level.

 Crutchfield faces four third-degree felony counts, each carrying a $20,000 warrant. He resigned from the Fort Pierce Police Department last month after learning he was under investigation. His bond remains set at $80,000.

hero.headline: K-9 Tobi alerts deputies to heroin, marijuana in Indian River County traffic stop
hero.teaser:
A traffic stop for a minor violation in Indian River County led to drug charges after a police dog detected narcotics in the vehicle, according to the sheriff's office.

Sheriff's
hero.body:
A traffic stop for a minor violation in Indian River County led to drug charges after a police dog detected narcotics in the vehicle, according to the sheriff's office.

 Sheriff's office road patrol deputies pulled over a vehicle Sunday night for a minor traffic infraction. K-9 Tobi was brought to the scene and alerted to the presence of drugs. Deputies discovered the vehicle had more than just the illegal window tint that prompted the initial stop.

 Substances that appeared to be marijuana tested positive for heroin as well, according to authorities. Jean Baptiste was taken into custody and faces multiple charges, including possession with intent to sell.

 The sheriff's office praised the work of the deputies and K-9 Tobi in a Facebook post, saying they did great work keeping the streets safe at night.
